Cancer relapse prediction from micro array data

The dataset contains 97 observations with 44 cases of relapse. And 754 gene expressions are recarded.

We can start by computing the signal over noise ratio of the gene expressions

# Function to find the genes with the highest SNR
genes_SNR = function(X,y){
  # - Inputs
  # X = dataset
  # y = labels (a boolean or factor variable)
  # - Output
  # SNR
  labels = unique(y)
  n = dim(X)[1]
  p = dim(X)[2]
  K = length(labels)
  
  means = matrix(0,length(labels),dim(X)[2])
  std = apply(X,2,sd)
  
  for (k in 1:K){means[k,] = apply(X[y==labels[k],],2,mean)}
  SNR = apply(matrix(abs(apply(means,2,diff)),K-1,p),2,max)/std
  return(SNR)
}

X_SNR = genes_SNR(X,y)
plot(X_SNR,typ="l")

library(ggplot2)

We work only with the genes which are differentially expressed. Some tests have been done previously and the AUC for boosting and bagging fit on all the genes is equal to 0.86.

w = which(X_SNR/max(X_SNR)>.6)
print(paste("Number of variables kept :",length(w)))
## [1] "Number of variables kept : 213"
X = X[,w]
cancer_relapse_select = data.frame(X)
cancer_relapse_select$y = y

Bagging

We use the treebag algorithm available in caret. Take care the computational time is quite long...

treebag_grid <-  expand.grid(k = c(1, 2, 5, 10))
                        
set.seed(825)
fitControl <- trainControl(## 5-fold CV
                           method = "repeatedcv",
                           number = 5, # nb of folds
                           ## repeated 1 times
                           repeats = 1) # repeat should be increased...
treebagFit <- train(y ~ ., data = cancer_relapse_select, 
                 preProcess=c("center", "scale"),
                 method = "treebag", 
                 metric = "Accuracy", 
                 verbose = TRUE, 
                 trControl = fitControl,
                 allowParallel=TRUE)
treebagFit
## Bagged CART 
## 
##  97 samples
## 213 predictors
##   2 classes: '0', '1' 
## 
## Pre-processing: centered (213), scaled (213) 
## Resampling: Cross-Validated (5 fold, repeated 1 times) 
## Summary of sample sizes: 78, 78, 77, 78, 77 
## Resampling results:
## 
##   Accuracy   Kappa    
##   0.8431579  0.6752008
treebagFit$finalModel
## 
## Bagging classification trees with 25 bootstrap replications
vip::vip(treebagFit, num_features = 20)

THe training selects a bagging with 25 trees. Lets us train such an ensemble and plot the ROC curve.

n = length(y)
itrain = sample(1:n,round(n*2/3))
itest = setdiff(1:n,itrain)
treebag = bagging(y ~ ., data = cancer_relapse, nbagg=25, control=
                 rpart.control(minsplit=2, cp=0, xval=0),subset = itrain)
y.prob.test = predict(treebag,cancer_relapse,typ="prob")[itest,2]
res_roc = roc(y[itest],y.prob.test)
## Setting levels: control = 0, case = 1
## Setting direction: controls < cases
plot(res_roc,xlim=c(1,0),ylim=c(0,1)) # ROC curve
text(.5,.2,paste("AUC =",round(res_roc$auc,2)))

The ROC curve is not smooth because only a few samples are considred in the test set. To improve the smoothness the experience can be repeated and the ROC curve plot for the concatenation of all the results.

Computation of the bagging may be long... Paralelization could be used.

B = 10
y.test = y.prob.test = NULL
for (b in 1:B){
  itrain = sample(1:n,round(n*2/3))
  itest = setdiff(1:n,itrain)
  treebag = bagging(y ~ ., data = cancer_relapse, nbagg=25, control=
                   rpart.control(minsplit=2, cp=0, xval=0),subset = itrain)
  y.test = c(y.test,y[itest])
  y.prob.test = c(y.prob.test,predict(treebag,cancer_relapse,typ="prob")[itest,2])
}
res_roc = roc(y.test,y.prob.test)
## Setting levels: control = 1, case = 2
## Setting direction: controls < cases
library(ggplot2)
g <- ggroc(res_roc)
g + xlab("FPR") + ylab("TPR") + 
    geom_segment(aes(x = 1, xend = 0, y = 0, yend = 1), color="darkgrey", linetype="dashed")

print(paste("Bagging, AUC =",round(res_roc$auc,2)))
## [1] "Bagging, AUC = 0.87"

y.test = y.prob.test = NULL
for (b in 1:B){
  itrain = sample(1:n,round(n*2/3))
  itest = setdiff(1:n,itrain)
  treeboost = ada(X[itrain,], y[itrain],loss="exponential",
     type=c("discrete"),iter=50, nu=1, bag.frac=0.3)
  y.test = c(y.test,y[itest])
  y.prob.test = c(y.prob.test,predict(treeboost,cancer_relapse,typ="prob")[itest,2])
}
res_roc_boost = roc(y.test,y.prob.test)
## Setting levels: control = 1, case = 2
## Setting direction: controls < cases
g_boost <- ggroc(res_roc_boost)
g_boost + xlab("FPR") + ylab("TPR") + 
    geom_segment(aes(x = 1, xend = 0, y = 0, yend = 1), color="darkgrey", linetype="dashed")

print(paste("Boosting, AUC =",round(res_roc$auc,2)))
## [1] "Boosting, AUC = 0.87"

Comparison

g2 <- ggroc(list(bagging=res_roc, RF=res_roc_rf, boosting=res_roc_boost))
